The '''Dwelling of Guests''' was a small building in the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quethold]]'s [[Red City]] that was built by [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]]. The circular building was filled with artwork owned by the ruler of the [[City/Legends|City]], the [[Queen of the Red]], which was replaced by the [[Storm-hair]] [[Species/Legends|species']], whose leader was the [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen's]] ally, [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]], in 8 ABY. The monarch's [[bowlcarrier]], [[Trevik]], was tasked with recording the Storm-hair artwork so that [[Empire of the Hand]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]&mdash;who could read a person's "hidden [[Heart/Legends|heart]]" by studying their artwork&mdash;could determine if the Queen was a willing ally of Esva's.

Esva had in fact selected paintings that would confuse Thrawn and therefore prompt him to execute a strategy adapted to the artwork that would give the warlord the upper hand in the coming [[Attack on the Red City|battle]] against the Grand Admiral. However, the Imperial knew of the other's plot, and changed his strategy mid-battle, shortly before Esva feared the Queen of the Red was a traitor and killed him in fear within the Dwelling.

==Description==
The Dwelling of Guests was a circular building situated in the center of the courtyard of the [[Palace (Red City)|Palace]]&mdash;inhabited by the [[Quesoth]] [[Species/Legends|species']] ruler, the [[Queen of the Red]]&mdash;in the [[Red City]] of the<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} — Based on corresponding data for [[Quethold system/Legends|Quethold system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Quethold]].<ref name="Crisis of Faith" /> Built by [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="Construction" /> it was small, containing a central gathering area on the ground floor and ten small quarters on the Dwelling's second floor. The [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen]] possessed several meditation which [[Gender/Legends|she]] planted in several chambers and walkways within the Dwelling. Objects also hung from the patterned walls. The building's furniture was built for the Quesoth's comfort, as their insectoid body required specifically shaped furniture.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==History==
{{Quote|So that's it.''"<br />"''<s></s>''[&hellip;]'' That's it. ''[&hellip;]'' One of the bodies in the Dwelling of Guests was positively identified as his.|Senior Captain Voss Parck and Grand Admiral Thrawn|<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />}}
In 8 ABY,<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'' to [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]].</ref> when the species known to the Quesoth as the [[Storm-hair]]s became the Queen of the Red's allies, her previous allies, the [[Stromma]] species, left the Dwelling so that the Storm-hairs could move in. As the Storm-hairs were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] and the Quesoth furniture were built for insectoids, they changed the furniture to their own, and changed the building's decoration significantly. One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], as the Queen's entourage entered the Dwelling, a [[Unidentified Chosen (Quethold)|Storm-hair]] [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|Chosen]] [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]] pledged his life to the Queen of the Red as mandated by Quesoth customs, and the leader of the Chosen, [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]], then spoke with the monarch.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

[[File:Thrawn-Hasbro.png|thumb|right|300px|Grand Admiral Thrawn, who attacked Quethold's Red City.]]
After leaving the Dwelling, the Queen's [[bowlcarrier]], [[Trevik]], who carried a bowl of [[Nectar/Legends|nectar]] for her, the bowlcarrier was intercepted by a [[Unidentified Circling|Circling]], one of the Queen of the Red's advisors. The Circling, along with Trevik's [[Trevik's family|brother]], [[Jirvin]], convinced the bowlcarrier to record the Storm-hair [[Painting/Legends|paintings]] within the Dwelling so that [[Empire of the Hand]] [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]&mdash;known for his ability to learn an enemy's strategy or intentions by studying their art&mdash;could determine if the Quesoth ruler was not being forced to ally herself with Esva. Unbeknownst to Trevik, the warlord had tasked Jirvin and the Circling to convince him to do so so that Thrawn's strategy would be made according to the paintings that Esva had chosen, and the Grand Admiral's coming [[Attack on the Red City|attack]] on the Red City would fail.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

The Chiss planned the strategy as the Storm-hair desired, and used it in his attack; however, during the battle that erupted between the [[Quesoth Soldier]]s and the Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], he changed his strategy, leading to his opponent's defeat. After killing the Queen and her entourage, including [[Circling]] [[Borosiv]], Esva was killed inside the Dwelling by Thrawn's forces.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

The next morning, Thrawn's forces attacked the city as Esva desired, however, Thrawn had predicted his opponent's plot and changed his strategy during the battle, defeating the warlord after he [[Death/Legends|killed]] the Queen and several Quesoth officials including Borosiv. Shortly after, Esva was killed inside the building by Thrawn's stormtroopers.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Dwelling of Guests appeared in the novella ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'', written by [[Timothy Zahn]] and published in [[2011]] as part of the [[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition|20th Anniversary Edition]] of the [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''.<ref name="Crisis of Faith" />
